fatal_errors: The proposed Hf-to-Al substitution does not reconstruct the target intervention of adding 4.2 at.% Cr by vacuum arc melting.
The hypothesis requires retention of a single BCC phase, whereas the target strengthening and ductility mechanism depends on approximately 4 vol.% of a reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase.

For Al0.2Hf0.8MoTaTiZr, only one-fifth of the Hf component is replaced; the asserted 10–15% density decrease is not justified by composition or cited evidence and is likely substantially overestimated.
The most relevant cited Al-addition evidence reports significant plasticity deterioration, directly weakening the claim that mechanical performance will be preserved.
explanation: The proposal addresses the broad density–strength trade-off and supplies explicit compression conditions, a compositional series, controls, and quantitative rejection thresholds, so it is experimentally useful as an alternative alloy-design hypothesis. It does not, however, recover the paper's Cr-addition intervention, interconnected Laves-phase mediator, dual solid-solution/crack-arrest mechanism, lattice contraction boundary, or simultaneous increases in room-temperature yield strength and fracture strain. Its evidence supports the general idea that Al can reduce RHEA density, but does not support retention of a single BCC phase or approximately 800 MPa yield strength at 1000 °C in this Mo–Ta-containing alloy. The falsification rule is also lenient relative to the stated 10–15% density prediction, rejecting only below 5%. Thus, it is a testable but weakly supported alternative rather than a reconstruction.
